method: Union of HEAD and current exact item-ID references anywhere in item carriers (including deps and wikilinks); breadth-first transitive closure; page uses scanned in both versions. Every listed use is literal carrier text.
before_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of finite graphs, and let $H_1,H_2\in
\mathcal F$. For $i=1,2$, let $v_i$ be a leaf of $H_i$, and write
$H_i':=H_i\setminus\{v_i\}$. If

$$\mathcal F_1:=\{H_1'\}\cup(\mathcal F\setminus\{H_1\})$$

and

$$\mathcal F_2:=\{H_2'\}\cup(\mathcal F\setminus\{H_2\})$$

are both viral, then $\mathcal F$ is viral.
current_statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite family of finite graphs, and let $H_1,H_2\in
\mathcal F$. Suppose $v_1$ is a leaf of $H_1$ and $v_2$ is a leaf of
$\overline{H_2}$. Put $H_i'=H_i-v_i$ for $i=1,2$. If

$$\mathcal F_1:=\{H_1'\}\cup(\mathcal F\setminus\{H_1\}),\qquad \mathcal F_2:=\{H_2'\}\cup(\mathcal F\setminus\{H_2\})$$

are viral, then $\mathcal F$ is viral.
